title: Illinois Driver's Car Freaks Out Before a Strange Light Appears
excerpt: A driver in rural Illinois recently reported their vehicle had weird electronic disturbances right before a strange light appeared.
content:
There's a new UFO report in Illinois that sounds very similar to one of the most famous scenes in the movie "Close Encounters of the Third Kind". A driver in rural Illinois had their vehicle begin to experience all kinds of electrical problems right before a light appeared above them.

This intriguing new eyewitness report on the National UFO Reporting Center site comes from the Williamsfield, Illinois area. Based on their statement, it happened late at night on October 12 between Williamsfield and Elmore, Illinois.

Here are the exact words of this eyewitness:

"Electrical disturbance with vehicle and phone. Followed by a light that was moving erratically. While driving the car lights started surging inside and outside. The cruise control cut off and the phone started behaving strangely. Apps were opening and closing followed by a disconnection of blue tooth. Seconds later a light appeared. At first it was very high and distant, almost like a star but slightly larger which made it stand out. As light was being observed it started getting bigger and closer very quickly. The light then found its way over a field and started moving in ways that that didn’t seem logical for any kind of aircraft and was too big to have been a drone. It hovered around and the light appeared to fade between a bright white and blueish white color. Shortly after the light started to speed away and then disappeared completely."

If you're not familiar with the Williamsfield, Illinois area, it's located to the northwest of Peoria. There are no airports anywhere near this part of the state. You can see the night sky clear as a bell most evenings. There are no known aircraft that move like this person described. I'd be very suspicious of the intentions of whatever this person saw that caused their vehicle to go crazy. This is the most Close Encounters of the Third Kind thing I've heard of in Illinois - ever.
